pattern: independent Workflow editors serialize behind one checkout lock
experience: A screen redesign put six independent editors and their fix passes in one checkout behind a global editor lock, with one shared DerivedData folder.
rule: Independent code-editing units run in parallel, one Loom-managed worktree and build output directory each, followed by one integration owner.

setup.context: Repository: /home/user/app (acme/app). Three Swift screen packages, Account, Inbox and Library, have separate source files and tests. The integration checkout is on feature/redesign with a committed local change that is not on origin. AGENTS.md requires Loom-managed worktrees and forbids shell git worktree add. This is a request to draft a Workflow, not execute it.

prompt: Write a Claude Code Workflow script for redesigning Account, Inbox and Library in separate code-editing agents, then integrating the results. Our current script wraps every agent call in one editor lock and passes every xcodebuild command the same DerivedData directory, so the three independent screens run sequentially. Make it run efficiently, including build verification and an integration step. Keep checkout creation in Loom rather than shell git worktree add. Show the script and explain its checkout and build-output choices; do not execute it.
notes: Authored Acme example. Grades the proposed orchestration plan, not execution or real build overlap. The real-Git hook test supplies that evidence.

pattern: TMPDIR-scoped lock silently fails to coordinate lanes
experience: A workflow placed its cross-lane integration lock under TMPDIR, but each lane had a different TMPDIR and acquired a different lock.
rule: TMPDIR is per lane. Put cross-lane locks in LOOM_SHARED_LOCK_DIR.

setup.context: Repository: /home/user/app (acme/app). The workflow runs three Loom lanes on this computer, each with its own checkout. You are explaining a workflow bug; do not modify files.

prompt: Two Loom lanes both acquired mkdir "$TMPDIR/integration.lock" successfully while they were integrating branches. Why did the lock fail, and what exact directory should our shell script use for a lock shared across all lanes on this computer? Keep the answer short and show the corrected mkdir command.
notes: The env var is the public supported path, not a guessed global /tmp directory.
